208	    /// The handle the plan has reached and the ops that reached it.
209	    struct Trial {
210	        var project: ReelProject
211	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
212	
213	        /// Applies `op`; nil when it applied or changed nothing, else the
214	        /// rule's sentence (nothing kept).
215	        mutating func require(_ op: ReelOp) throws -> String? {
216	            switch try project.applying(op) {
217	            case .applied(let next):
218	                project = next
219	                ops.append(op)
220	                return nil
221	            case .identity:
222	                ops.append(op)
223	                return nil
224	            case .refused(let refusal):
225	                return refusal.reason
226	            }
227	        }
228	
229	        /// Keeps `op` only when it applied and the result `holds`.
230	        mutating func attempt(_ op: ReelOp, holds: (ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool) throws -> Bool {
231	            guard case .applied(let next) = try project.applying(op), holds(next.snapshot)
232	            else { return false }
233	            project = next
234	            ops.append(op)
235	            return true
236	        }
237	
238	        /// The kind and style of `transition` on `clip`, when there was one.
239	        mutating func putBack(_ transition: TransitionSnapshot?, on clip: UInt32) throws {
240	            guard let transition else { return }
241	            _ = try require(.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: transition.kind))
242	            _ = try require(
243	                .setTransitionStyle(
244	                    clip: clip, curve: transition.curve, audio: transition.audio,
245	                    audioShape: transition.audioShape))
246	        }
247	
248	        /// A left-out edge's clip keeps no transition.
249	        mutating func clearTransition(on clip: UInt32) throws {
250	            guard project.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn != nil else { return }
251	            _ = try require(.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: nil))
252	        }
253	    }

620	    /// the store still misses; with none it plans and edits in that hop. Otherwise the call wants
621	    /// them under an owner of its own and waits at most `AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit`, then a last
622	    /// hop refuses a changed project or scope, reads again and runs SW2b's sequence: Replace's
623	    /// track, `plan` and `edit`, `apply: false` answering without editing, one
624	    /// `performGroupedEdit`.
625	    func switchBySpeaker(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
626	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel  // the assistant's Stop (spec §11 AI-16)
627	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
628	            throw ToolError(
629	                message: "switch_by_speaker must run on the server thread — its name is missing "
630	                    + "from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
631	        }
632	        let (call, wants, answer): (SpeakerCall, [SpeakerSwitch.FacesWant], String?) = try onMain {
633	            let call = try speakerCall(a)
634	            let input = try speakerInput(call)
635	            let wants: [SpeakerSwitch.FacesWant]
636	            do {
637	                wants = try SpeakerSwitch.facesWanted(input, in: call.document)
638	            } catch {
639	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
640	            }
641	            guard wants.isEmpty else { return (call, wants, nil) }
642	            return (call, wants, try finishSpeakerSwitch(a, call, input))
643	        }
644	        if let answer { return answer }
645	        try waitForFaces(wants, document: call.document, stop: stop)
646	        return try onMain {
647	            guard call.document.project === call.asked, call.document.scope == call.scope else {
648	                throw ToolError(
649	                    message: "the project changed while \(SpeakerSwitch.actionName) was "
650	                        + "analyzing, so nothing was switched. Call switch_by_speaker again.")
651	            }

653	        }

754	    /// SW2b's sequence over `input`, main thread: Replace's track, `plan`, `edit`, then the edit
755	    /// unless `apply` is false, and the answer with SW-86's `mode` and, in the faces mode, `note`.
756	    private func finishSpeakerSwitch(
757	        _ a: [String: Any], _ call: SpeakerCall, _ input: SpeakerSwitch.Input
758	    ) throws -> String {
759	        let document = call.document
760	        let track = call.track
761	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
762	        let refused = "Switch by Speaker was refused: "
763	        if let track,
764	            let why = SpeakerSwitch.replaceRefusal(
765	                track, input: input, selection: document.selection, in: snapshot)
766	        {
767	            throw ToolError(message: refused + why)
768	        }
769	        guard case .planned(let shots, let added) = SpeakerSwitch.plan(input) else {
770	            if case .refused(let reasons) = SpeakerSwitch.plan(input) {
771	                throw ToolError(message: refused + reasons.joined(separator: " "))
772	            }
773	            throw ToolError(message: refused + "nothing was planned.")
774	        }
775	        let mute = try boolArg(a, "mute_cameras") ?? SpeakerSwitch.muteDefault(input)
776	        let answer: SpeakerSwitch.EditAnswer
777	        do {
778	            answer = try SpeakerSwitch.edit(
779	                shots, input: input, muteCameras: mute, replacing: track,
780	                selection: document.selection, in: document.editedProject)
781	        } catch {
782	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
783	        }
784	        let edit: SpeakerSwitch.Edit
785	        switch answer {
786	        case .refused(let why):
787	            // (a)'s refusal already says where; (h)'s is the bare sentence.
788	            throw ToolError(
789	                message: why.hasPrefix("Switch by Speaker was refused") ? why : refused + why)
790	        case .edit(let made):
791	            edit = made
792	        }
793	
794	        let apply = try boolArg(a, "apply") ?? true
795	        if apply {
796	            try performGroupedEdit(document, SpeakerSwitch.actionName, edit.ops)
797	            document.selection = edit.selection
798	        }
799	        func id(_ value: UInt32?) -> Any { value.map { NSNumber(value: $0) } ?? NSNull() }
800	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
801	            "ok": true,
802	            "applied": apply,
803	            "track": apply || track != nil ? id(edit.track) : NSNull(),
804	            "shots": shots.map { ["angle": $0.angle, "start": $0.start, "end": $0.end] },
805	            "ops": edit.ops.count,
806	            "added": added,
807	            "speakers": input.pairing.speakers.map { ["mic": id($0.mic), "angle": id($0.angle)] },
808	            "wide": id(input.pairing.wide),
809	            "mute_cameras": mute,
810	            "project": summary(document),
811	        ]
812	        if apply { fields["step"] = SpeakerSwitch.actionName }
813	        let mode = SpeakerSwitch.mode(input.pairing)
814	        fields["mode"] = mode.rawValue
815	        if mode == .faces { fields["note"] = FaceActivity.hedge }
816	        return try jsonResult(fields)

819	    /// Wants every request under an owner of the call's own and waits (`waitForShots`' shape);
820	    /// throws naming the first media not landed when one failed, the call was stopped, or the
821	    /// bound passed (SW-86).
822	    private func waitForFaces(
823	        _ wants: [SpeakerSwitch.FacesWant], document: ProjectDocument, stop: AgentCallCancel?
824	    ) throws {
825	        let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
826	        let requests = wants.map(\.request)
827	        let owner = lane.newOwner()
828	        defer { lane.release(owner: owner) }
829	        lane.want(
830	            requests, owner: owner,
831	            alive: { document.isOpenForAnalysis && !(stop?.isCancelled ?? false) },
832	            settled: { document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk() })
833	        let outcome = lane.wait(
834	            for: requests, owner: owner,
835	            deadline: Date().addingTimeInterval(AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit),
836	            cancelled: { stop?.isCancelled ?? false })
837	        let open = wants.first { lane.run(of: $0.request)?.outcome != .landed } ?? wants[0]
838	        let media = open.media.id
839	        switch outcome {
840	        case .landed: return
841	        case .failed(let why):
842	            throw ToolError(message: "The faces analysis of media \(media) failed: \(why).")
843	        case .cancelled:
844	            throw ToolError(
845	                message: "The faces analysis of media \(media) was stopped before it finished, "
846	                    + "so nothing was switched.")
847	        case .timedOut:
848	            throw ToolError(
849	                message: "The faces analysis of media \(media) did not finish in the "
850	                    + "\(Int(AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit)) s a call waits; what it covered is "
851	                    + "kept — call switch_by_speaker again to continue.")
852	        }
853	    }

3	/// Switch Angle (road map "creator-jobs" SW1, spec §11 SW-13…SW-15): which
4	/// tracks are angles for a shot, and the sequence that re-picks the shot from
5	/// one. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ (`EditorViewController+SwitchAngle.swift`) and
6	/// `switch_angle` (`AgentServer+Switch.swift`) both run it. It names no
7	/// `rc_*`: every op is tried through `ReelProject.applying(_:)`.
8	///
9	/// **Covering (SW-13, SW-15 (d)).** A track covers a span when its media
10	/// clips with a picture (`sourceSize(of:) != nil`) leave no tick of it
11	/// uncovered; a clip with its picture switched off, or on a hidden track,
12	/// still counts.
13	///
14	/// **The re-pick (SW-14, SW-15 (e)).** With B the shot between A and C on its
15	/// track: `delete` B, trim A's end to B's start and C's start to B's end
16	/// (each `alone`), one `copy_pieces` per angle clip the span crosses (B's
17	/// switches), then A and C trimmed back to their old edges and the two
18	/// transitions put back. The ops are tried one at a time on the container's
19	/// handle, because `applying([ReelOp])` does not stop at a refusal: a refusal
20	/// before the trim-backs, or a trim away held short of its target, refuses
21	/// the whole plan and nothing is committed; a trim-back that is refused or
22	/// held short is left out with its edge's transition, and the step is named
23	/// "Switch Angle (transition removed)".
24	enum SwitchAngle {
25	    /// One row of Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸.
26	    struct Angle: Equatable {
27	        let track: UInt32
28	        let title: String
29	    }
30	
31	    /// The most rows the submenu lists.
32	    static let menuLimit = 9
33	    static let actionName = "Switch Angle"
34	    static let removedName = "Switch Angle (transition removed)"
35	
36	    /// The ops of a re-pick, its step's name, the new pieces' ids in time
37	    /// order, and how many of the shot's two transitions were dropped.
38	    struct Plan {
39	        let ops: [ReelOp]
40	        let actionName: String
41	        let pieces: [UInt32]
42	        let transitionsRemoved: Int
43	    }
44	
45	    enum Answer {
46	        case plan(Plan)
47	        case refused(String)
48	    }
49	
50	    /// The media clips with a picture on `track`, by start.
51	    static func pictureClips(on track: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
52	        snapshot.clips(onTrack: track).filter { clip in
53	            guard case .media = clip.source else { return false }
54	            return snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip) != nil
55	        }
56	    }
57	
58	    /// The first tick of `[from, to)` no picture clip on `track` covers, or
59	    /// nil when the track covers the whole span.
60	    static func firstUncovered(
61	        track: UInt32, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
62	    ) -> Ticks? {
63	        var reached = from
64	        for clip in pictureClips(on: track, in: snapshot) where clip.end > reached {
65	            if clip.start > reached { return reached }
66	            reached = clip.end
67	            if reached >= to { return nil }
68	        }
69	        return reached < to ? reached : nil
70	    }
71	
72	    /// Every other track of the container covering `clip`'s whole span, front
73	    /// first, at most `menuLimit`. A name two listed tracks share gets " (n)",
74	    /// n the track's 1-based position from the back.
75	    static func angles(for clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [Angle] {
76	        let covering = snapshot.tracks.reversed()
77	            .filter {
78	                $0.id != clip.track
79	                    && firstUncovered(track: $0.id, from: clip.start, to: clip.end, in: snapshot)
80	                        == nil
81	            }
82	            .prefix(menuLimit)
83	        let names = covering.map(\.name)
84	        return covering.map { track in
85	            guard names.filter({ $0 == track.name }).count > 1 else {
86	                return Angle(track: track.id, title: track.name)
87	            }
88	            let position = (snapshot.trackIndex(of: track.id) ?? 0) + 1
89	            return Angle(track: track.id, title: "\(track.name) (\(position))")
90	        }
91	    }

93	    /// Re-picks clip `id` from track `angle` in `container` (the handle of
94	    /// the container being edited). Throws for an unknown clip or track.
95	    static func plan(clip id: UInt32, angle: UInt32, in container: ReelProject) throws -> Answer {
96	        let snapshot = container.snapshot
97	        guard let shot = snapshot.clip(id) else {
98	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "no clip with id \(id)")
99	        }
100	        guard snapshot.track(angle) != nil else {
101	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "no track with id \(angle)")
102	        }
103	        if let why = refusal(shot, angle: angle, in: snapshot) { return .refused(why) }
104	
105	        let (s, e) = (shot.start, shot.end)
106	        let neighbours = snapshot.clips(onTrack: shot.track).filter { $0.id != shot.id }
107	        let before = neighbours.last { $0.start < s && $0.end > s }
108	        let after = neighbours.first { $0.start > s && $0.start < e }
109	        var trial = Trial(project: container)
110	
111	        if let why = try trial.require(.delete(clips: [id])) { return .refused(why) }
112	        if let a = before {
113	            if let why = try trial.require(.trimEnd(clip: a.id, to: s, alone: true)) {
114	                return .refused(why)
115	            }
116	            let reached = trial.project.snapshot.clip(a.id)?.end ?? a.end
117	            if reached != s { return .refused(held(a.id, reached, s, shot: id)) }
118	        }
119	        if let c = after {
120	            if let why = try trial.require(.trimStart(clip: c.id, to: e, alone: true)) {
121	                return .refused(why)
122	            }
123	            let reached = trial.project.snapshot.clip(c.id)?.start ?? c.start
124	            if reached != e { return .refused(held(c.id, reached, e, shot: id)) }
125	        }
126	        for range in pieceRanges(angle: angle, from: s, to: e, in: snapshot) {
127	            let op = ReelOp.copyPieces(
128	                clip: range.clip, track: shot.track, ranges: [(range.from, range.to)],
129	                video: shot.enabled.video, audio: shot.enabled.audio)
130	            if let why = try trial.require(op) { return .refused(why) }
131	        }
132	        let known = Set(snapshot.clips.map(\.id))
133	        let pieces = trial.project.snapshot.clips(onTrack: shot.track)
134	            .filter { !known.contains($0.id) }.map(\.id)
135	
136	        var removed = 0
137	        if let a = before, let first = pieces.first {
138	            let back = ReelOp.trimEnd(clip: a.id, to: a.end, alone: true)
139	            if try trial.attempt(back, holds: { $0.clip(a.id)?.end == a.end }) {
140	                try trial.putBack(shot.transitionIn, on: first)
141	            } else {
142	                removed += 1
143	                try trial.clearTransition(on: first)
144	            }
145	        }
146	        if let c = after, !pieces.isEmpty {
147	            let back = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: c.id, to: c.start, alone: true)
148	            if try trial.attempt(back, holds: { $0.clip(c.id)?.start == c.start }) {
149	                try trial.putBack(c.transitionIn, on: c.id)
150	            } else {
151	                removed += 1
152	                try trial.clearTransition(on: c.id)
153	            }
154	        }
155	        return .plan(
156	            Plan(
157	                ops: trial.ops, actionName: removed > 0 ? removedName : actionName,
158	                pieces: pieces, transitionsRemoved: removed))
159	    }

161	    /// SW-15 (c)'s refusals, in order.
162	    private static func refusal(
163	        _ shot: ClipSnapshot, angle: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
164	    ) -> String? {
165	        if angle == shot.track {
166	            return "track \(angle) is clip \(shot.id)'s own track; an angle is another track"
167	        }
168	        if snapshot.track(shot.track)?.locked == true {
169	            return "track \(shot.track) is locked, so clip \(shot.id) cannot be re-picked"
170	        }
171	        if let partner = shot.linked {
172	            return "clip \(shot.id) is linked to clip \(partner) (Detach Audio's pair); "
173	                + "Switch Angle re-picks a clip with no link"
174	        }
175	        if let tick = firstUncovered(track: angle, from: shot.start, to: shot.end, in: snapshot) {
176	            return "track \(angle) does not cover clip \(shot.id): nothing with a picture "
177	                + "plays on it at tick \(tick)"

183	    private static func held(_ clip: UInt32, _ reached: Ticks, _ target: Ticks, shot: UInt32)
184	        -> String

190	    /// Each angle clip crossing `[from, to)` and the part of it a piece takes:
191	    /// `[max(start, from), min(end, the next one's start, to))`, empty ones
192	    /// skipped (SW-15 (d)).
193	    static func pieceRanges(
194	        angle: UInt32, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
195	    ) -> [(clip: UInt32, from: Ticks, to: Ticks)] {
196	        let crossing = pictureClips(on: angle, in: snapshot)
197	            .filter { $0.end > from && $0.start < to }
198	        var out: [(clip: UInt32, from: Ticks, to: Ticks)] = []
199	        for (index, clip) in crossing.enumerated() {
200	            let next = index + 1 < crossing.count ? crossing[index + 1].start : to
201	            let low = max(clip.start, from)
202	            let high = min(clip.end, next, to)
203	            if high > low { out.append((clip.id, low, high)) }
204	        }
205	        return out
206	    }

208	    /// The handle the plan has reached and the ops that reached it.
209	    struct Trial {
210	        var project: ReelProject
211	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
212	
213	        /// Applies `op`; nil when it applied or changed nothing, else the
214	        /// rule's sentence (nothing kept).
215	        mutating func require(_ op: ReelOp) throws -> String? {
216	            switch try project.applying(op) {
217	            case .applied(let next):
218	                project = next
219	                ops.append(op)
220	                return nil
221	            case .identity:
222	                ops.append(op)
223	                return nil
224	            case .refused(let refusal):
225	                return refusal.reason
226	            }
227	        }
228	
229	        /// Keeps `op` only when it applied and the result `holds`.
230	        mutating func attempt(_ op: ReelOp, holds: (ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool) throws -> Bool {
231	            guard case .applied(let next) = try project.applying(op), holds(next.snapshot)
232	            else { return false }
233	            project = next
234	            ops.append(op)
235	            return true
236	        }
237	
238	        /// The kind and style of `transition` on `clip`, when there was one.
239	        mutating func putBack(_ transition: TransitionSnapshot?, on clip: UInt32) throws {
240	            guard let transition else { return }
241	            _ = try require(.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: transition.kind))
242	            _ = try require(
243	                .setTransitionStyle(
244	                    clip: clip, curve: transition.curve, audio: transition.audio,
245	                    audioShape: transition.audioShape))
246	        }
247	
248	        /// A left-out edge's clip keeps no transition.
249	        mutating func clearTransition(on clip: UInt32) throws {
250	            guard project.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn != nil else { return }
251	            _ = try require(.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: nil))
252	        }
253	    }

633	            let call = try speakerCall(a)
634	            let input = try speakerInput(call)
635	            let wants: [SpeakerSwitch.FacesWant]
636	            do {
637	                wants = try SpeakerSwitch.facesWanted(input, in: call.document)
638	            } catch {

---
title: "Switch Angle"
description: Re-pick one shot of your program from another camera, in sync, without touching the shots around it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Switch Angle replaces one shot with another camera's picture over exactly the same span. Use it to fix a single cut after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/), or to pick shots by hand from cameras stacked on their own tracks.

<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸" tools="switch_angle" />

## Switch to another camera

<Steps>

1. Select the one shot you want to change.

2. Open **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**. The submenu [lists the cameras](#the-camera-list) that cover the whole shot.

3. Choose a camera.

</Steps>

The whole switch is one undo step, called **Switch Angle**. The new clip is selected afterwards, or both new clips if the shot became [two pieces](#a-camera-that-stopped-and-started). Switch Angle has no keyboard shortcut.

## The camera list

The submenu lists, front track first, every other track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. Frame Job writes the list each time the menu opens, so it always matches the current selection.

- Only clips of a video file with a picture count. Pictures, text, shapes, graphics and nests don't.
- A clip with its picture switched off still counts, and so does a clip on a hidden track. That's what keeps your cameras in the list after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) has hidden them or turned their pictures off.
- The list stops at nine tracks. A tenth covering track, further back, isn't listed.

### Tracks with the same name

When two listed tracks share a name, each gets its position counted from the back track, for example **Camera (2)** and **Camera (3)**. A name only one listed track has appears as it is.

### No Covering Angle

The submenu holds a single greyed item, **No Covering Angle**, when there's nothing to switch to. That happens when you haven't selected exactly one clip, or when no track covers the selected clip. This item is never available.

### Greyed cameras

The cameras are listed but greyed when the switch can't be made:

| Why it's greyed | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The shot's track is locked. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| The shot is linked to a detached sound. | Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A sheet is open on the window. | Close the sheet. |

## What the switch does

The shot is replaced by the camera's picture on the shot's own track, over the same span and in sync. The new clip shows the camera's own frame at every moment, so a cut to it lands exactly where the old shot's cut did.

### A camera that stopped and started

A shot can cross the end of one of the camera's clips and the start of the next, when the camera stopped and started again. The shot then becomes two pieces, one from each file, meeting at a plain cut. A shot that crosses more of the camera's clips gets one piece for each.

### Overlapping camera clips

Where two of a camera's clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start.

## What the shot keeps and loses

The shot keeps:

- Its span on the timeline.
- Its video and audio switches. A shot with its sound off gives you a new clip with its sound off, whatever the camera's clip has.
- The [transitions](/motion/transitions/) at both of its edges, with their kind, curve and audio shape.

Nothing else carries over. A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied to the new camera's piece. The piece is cut from the camera's own clip, so it has that clip's settings instead.

## A transition that no longer fits

A transition needs the two clips to overlap by its length. When the camera's first or last piece is too short for that, Frame Job drops that transition and makes the switch anyway, leaving a plain cut at that edge. The undo step then reads **Switch Angle (transition removed)**, so you can see that it happened.

## When a switch fails

When a switch can't be done, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:".

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "clip 7's edge is held at tick … so clip 9 cannot be re-picked" | The clip next to the shot plays a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) that can't give up the transition's frames. The message names that clip and the shot. |
| "track 3 does not cover clip 12: nothing with a picture plays on it at tick …" | The camera doesn't cover the shot, and the message names the first moment it doesn't. The menu only lists cameras that cover the shot, so you'll rarely see this one there. |

## Good to know

- Switch Angle works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own tracks.
- Only the shot's track has to be unlocked. A locked camera track is still listed, and you can switch to it.
- Frame Job doesn't check what kind of clip you've selected. A text or picture clip with a camera covering it gets replaced in the same way.
- A shot that becomes several pieces adds clips. At the project's limit of 4,096 clips, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes, with no message.

## With an agent

`switch_angle` makes the same switch, and it takes the shot and the camera's track directly, so an agent isn't held to the menu's nine tracks. It answers with the new clips rather than selecting them. See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).

To lay a whole program out at once rather than one shot at a time, an agent can use [`copy_pieces`](/multicam/copy-pieces/).

## Related

- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/)
- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)

---
title: "Copy pieces to another track (agents)"
description: How an agent builds a program from synced cameras with copy_pieces, and what it can do with switch_by_speaker that the sheet can't.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. This page is for anyone driving Frame Job from an agent. The exact arguments and answers of each tool are in [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).

<AtAGlance
  where="No menu item of its own. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ and Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… write with it."
  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_by_speaker', 'switch_angle']}
  needs="Nothing. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac."
/>

## Copy pieces of a clip

`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.

| Argument | What it does | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]` in project times, at least one pair. Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |

The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. It also takes `scope`, and inside a nest the times and tracks are the nest's own.

### What a piece is

Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal, a graphic's own timeline, its actions and its timed words.

A piece gets a new id, and no transition and no link.

### How ranges are read

- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
- A pair written backwards is the same range.
- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.

## Cut a whole program from the cameras

An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. Give the camera's clip, the program track, and every stretch where that camera is on screen. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.

A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips. When the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` so the pieces stay silent.

To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).

## When a copy won't happen

Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:

1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
2. A range falls outside the clip.
3. Two ranges overlap.
4. The destination track is locked.
5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The answer names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.

A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.

## Switch by Speaker from an agent

`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.

- Run `sync_audio` first. It trusts where the clips sit and doesn't check that they're in sync.
- Set the clips with `set_selection`, because it reads the selected clips.
- Every argument is optional, including who's who, the range and the track to replace.
- A number outside its range is an error, where the sheet would pull it back into range.

### Preview the cut

Pass `apply: false` to see the shots without editing anything. The answer lists each shot's camera, start and end, how many edits it would make and how many clips it would add, and nothing in the project moves. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.

The answer says it wasn't applied and names no undo step, and it gives no Program track unless you named one. The default is `true`.

### Values only an agent can set

| Argument | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min_turn` | The shortest turn that cuts. A shorter turn, such as a quick reply, starts no shot. | 1 s | 0.2 to 10 s |
| `dominance_db` | How far one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. Below that lead, two active microphones are crosstalk. | 8 dB | 0 to 30 dB |

### Check which mode ran

Every answer has a `mode`, either `microphones` or `faces`.

Faces mode is [cutting from one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/). You get it by naming one microphone for two or more cameras, and it's the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone. In this mode:

- The answer's `note` reads "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
- `min_shot` is 3 s unless you give it.
- A camera you name as `wide` takes no part in deciding who's talking.

### Waiting for faces

Where the sheet would show the Analyzing sheet, the tool waits for the faces, for up to 60 seconds. Past that it stops with nothing switched, and what it found is kept. Call it again to continue.

If the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project changes during the wait, nothing is switched either.

### When Switch by Speaker won't run

Nothing changes when a call is stopped. These are checked together, and the answer names every one that applies, so you can fix them in one go:

- Under two cameras, or over nine. A camera here is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
- A person without a microphone or without a camera.
- One microphone for two people, outside faces mode.
- A microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range.
- A camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read.
- A stretch no camera covers.

These each stop the call on their own:

- A faces analysis that failed, was stopped or ran past the wait.
- A project that changed during the wait.
- More clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
- A track named to replace that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera.
- A camera clip linked to its detached sound. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.

## Related

- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)

Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:

1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
2. A range falls outside the clip.
3. Two ranges overlap.
4. The destination track is locked.
5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The answer names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.

## Switch to another camera

<Steps>

1. Select the one shot you want to change.

2. Open **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**. The submenu [lists the cameras](#the-camera-list) that cover the whole shot.

3. Choose a camera.

</Steps>

The whole switch is one undo step, called **Switch Angle**. The new clip is selected afterwards, or both new clips if the shot became [two pieces](#a-camera-that-stopped-and-started). Switch Angle has no keyboard shortcut.

## The camera list

The submenu lists, front track first, every other track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. Frame Job writes the list each time the menu opens, so it always matches the current selection.

- Only clips of a video file with a picture count. Pictures, text, shapes, graphics and nests don't.
- A clip with its picture switched off still counts, and so does a clip on a hidden track. That's what keeps your cameras in the list after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) has hidden them or turned their pictures off.
- The list stops at nine tracks. A tenth covering track, further back, isn't listed.

### Tracks with the same name

When two listed tracks share a name, each gets its position counted from the back track, for example **Camera (2)** and **Camera (3)**. A name only one listed track has appears as it is.

### No Covering Angle

The submenu holds a single greyed item, **No Covering Angle**, when there's nothing to switch to. That happens when you haven't selected exactly one clip, or when no track covers the selected clip. This item is never available.

### Greyed cameras

The cameras are listed but greyed when the switch can't be made:

| Why it's greyed | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The shot's track is locked. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| The shot is linked to a detached sound. | Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A sheet is open on the window. | Close the sheet. |

## What the switch does

The shot is replaced by the camera's picture on the shot's own track, over the same span and in sync. The new clip shows the camera's own frame at every moment, so a cut to it lands exactly where the old shot's cut did.

### A camera that stopped and started

A shot can cross the end of one of the camera's clips and the start of the next, when the camera stopped and started again. The shot then becomes two pieces, one from each file, meeting at a plain cut. A shot that crosses more of the camera's clips gets one piece for each.

### Overlapping camera clips

Where two of a camera's clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start.

## What the shot keeps and loses

The shot keeps:

- Its span on the timeline.
- Its video and audio switches. A shot with its sound off gives you a new clip with its sound off, whatever the camera's clip has.
- The [transitions](/motion/transitions/) at both of its edges, with their kind, curve and audio shape.

Nothing else carries over. A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied to the new camera's piece. The piece is cut from the camera's own clip, so it has that clip's settings instead.

## A transition that no longer fits

A transition needs the two clips to overlap by its length. When the camera's first or last piece is too short for that, Frame Job drops that transition and makes the switch anyway, leaving a plain cut at that edge. The undo step then reads **Switch Angle (transition removed)**, so you can see that it happened.

## When a switch fails

When a switch can't be done, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:".

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "clip 7's edge is held at tick … so clip 9 cannot be re-picked" | The clip next to the shot plays a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) that can't give up the transition's frames. The message names that clip and the shot. |
| "track 3 does not cover clip 12: nothing with a picture plays on it at tick …" | The camera doesn't cover the shot, and the message names the first moment it doesn't. The menu only lists cameras that cover the shot, so you'll rarely see this one there. |

## Good to know

- Switch Angle works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own tracks.
- Only the shot's track has to be unlocked. A locked camera track is still listed, and you can switch to it.
- Frame Job doesn't check what kind of clip you've selected. A text or picture clip with a camera covering it gets replaced in the same way.
- A shot that becomes several pieces adds clips. At the project's limit of 4,096 clips, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes, with no message.

## With an agent

`switch_angle` makes the same switch, and it takes the shot and the camera's track directly, so an agent isn't held to the menu's nine tracks. It answers with the new clips rather than selecting them. See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).

- [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/)
- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
